## Claims
- [source-backed] The original paper conjectures that the two Theorem 5.4 generating sets for \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) are minimal, verified computationally only for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2, lines 1495-1502]
- [source-backed] Its proposed stronger form is \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}/\Lambda_+J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\), explicitly stated as unproved there. [source-2, lines 1536-1552]
- [source-backed] The targeted later candidate is Avery St. Dizier–Alexander Yong, *Presenting the cohomology of a Schubert variety: Proof of the minimality conjecture* (2024); its supplied abstract says “We prove the minimality conjecture” and attributes the proof to the Hopf-algebra structure of symmetric functions. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832]
- [unsupported] No exact theorem statement, locator, or hypotheses from the 2024 paper were supplied. Therefore its applicability to the current integral \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\), its two specified generating families, and the stronger free-abelian indecomposables statement is unverified.

## Strategy
Compared the original conjecture and stronger statement with the uniquely targeted 2024 title/abstract-level result.

## Gaps
The requested literature reduction is **not established**: abstract metadata does not verify whether the 2024 theorem proves minimality for every type-\(A\) bigrassmannian parameter set, nor whether it proves \(J/\Lambda_+J\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\).

## Next
